BHARAT MOTORS — CUSTOMER SERVICE POLICY MANUAL
SECTION 1: WARRANTY POLICY
1.1 Standard Warranty Coverage
All new Bharat Motors passenger vehicles carry a standard manufacturer warranty of
2 years or 40,000 km (whichever occurs first) from the date of vehicle delivery, as
recorded in the Owner Manual and digital Service Record.
1.2 What Is Covered
Engine assembly, transmission assembly, electrical systems (wiring harness, ECU,
sensors, infotainment unit), air conditioning compressor, suspension c

ess, ECU,
sensors, infotainment unit), air conditioning compressor, suspension components,
and paint/body panels (3 years) against manufacturing defects only.
1.3 What Is Not Covered
Normal wear-and-tear items (brake pads, clutch plates, wiper blades, tyres, bulbs),
damage from accidents/misuse/overloading/off-road use/unauthorized modifications,
damage from non-recommended fuel or accessories, and corrosion due to lack of
maintenance unless anti-rust warranty was separately purchased.
1.4 Exten

ack of
maintenance unless anti-rust warranty was separately purchased.
1.4 Extended Warranty
Available up to 5 years / 100,000 km if purchased within 40,000 km or 24 months of
delivery, whichever is earlier. Same coverage exclusions as standard warranty apply.
1.5 Warranty Claim Process
Claims must be raised at an authorized service center, supported by service history.
A single missed scheduled service does not automatically void warranty, but repeated
non-adherence may be cited if the defect i

non-adherence may be cited if the defect is directly linked to lack of maintenance.
Approval timelines are typically 3–7 working days after inspection.
1.6 Agent Limits on Warranty
Support agents CANNOT approve, reject, or guarantee warranty claim outcomes — only
the manufacturer's warranty approval team can decide after physical inspection.
Agents CANNOT waive exclusions or offer discretionary goodwill repairs; such
requests must be escalated to the service

SECTION 2: PERIODIC SERVICE SCHEDULE
2.1 Free Services
Service 1 at 1,000 km/1 month (inspection only, labour free); Service 2 at
5,000 km/6 months; Service 3 at 10,000 km/12 months. Free services cover labour
only; consumables beyond Service 1 are chargeable.

2.2 Paid Periodic Services
Every 10,000 km or 12 months thereafter. Includes engine oil/filter replacement,
air filter check (alternate services), brake inspection/fluid top-up, and a
40+ point multi-point health check.
2.3 Additional Scheduled Items
Cabin air filter every 15,000 km; brake fluid every 40,000 km/2 years; coolant
every 60,000 km/3 years. Timing belt/chain interval is engine-specific — agents
must direct customers to their model's Owner Manual or the service center rather
than quot

t customers to their model's Owner Manual or the service center rather
than quoting a generic number.
2.4 Agent Limits on Service
Agents CANNOT quote exact service cost estimates (varies by city, variant, and
current parts pricing) — use the cost-estimate tool or direct to service center.
Agents CANNOT guarantee specific appointment slots.
SECTION 3: RECALL POLICY
3.1 Recall Notification
Registered owners are notified by SMS, email, and registered post. Recalls are
published on the Bharat Motors

d by SMS, email, and registered post. Recalls are
published on the Bharat Motors official website.
3.2 Checking Recall Status
Use the vehicle's VIN (on the RC book / chassis) via the official recall-check
tool. Agents must NOT guess or assume recall status without checking.
3.3 Recall Repairs
Free of cost at authorized service centers regardless of warranty status.
3.4 Safety-Critical Symptoms
If a customer reports symptoms matching a known safety-recall category (airbag
malfunction, brake failu

ymptoms matching a known safety-recall category (airbag
malfunction, brake failure, steering issue, fuel leak, smoke/fire risk), the agent
MUST advise the customer to stop using the vehicle if there is immediate danger,
direct them to roadside assistance/emergency services, and escalate to a human
specialist immediately. Agents must NOT speculate on mechanical cause or suggest
DIY fixes for safety-critical symptoms.
SECTION 4: DATA PRIVACY
Customer PII (name, phone number, email, vehicle registr

SECTION 4: DATA PRIVACY
Customer PII (name, phone number, email, vehicle registration number, VIN, address)
must never be written to persistent conversation logs in plaintext. All logs must
store a redacted/masked form. PII may be held only in-memory for the duration of an
active session to fulfill the customer's request.

SECTION 5: PROHIBITED AGENT ACTIONS
Agents must never: process or promise refunds/discounts outside official promotions;
provide legal advice; share another customer's information; help a customer bypass
a safety recall or falsify a service record; or guarantee outcomes of claims,
inspections, or approvals that require human/manufacturer sign-off.

BHARAT MOTORS — CUSTOMER SUPPORT ESCALATION GUIDELINES
(INTERNAL / AGENT-FACING)
PURPOSE
These guidelines define when the AI support agent must stop attempting to resolve
a query itself and instead create an escalation ticket for a human specialist.
MANDATORY ESCALATION TRIGGERS
1. Safety-critical vehicle symptoms: brake failure, steering failure, airbag
deployment/malfunction, smoke, fire, fuel leak, or any symptom matching a known
recall safety category.
2. Active recall confirmed on the custo

matching a known
recall safety category.
2. Active recall confirmed on the customer's VIN — schedule the recall repair via
the service center and additionally flag for human confirmation of completion.
3. Legal, insurance-claim, or accident-liability questions — these require a human
claims specialist, not the support agent.
4. Requests for refunds, discounts, or fee waivers beyond standard published policy.
5. Repeated unresolved complaint (the same issue reported 2+ times) or visible
customer

customer frustration/anger indicating dissatisfaction with automated support.
6. Any request the agent cannot answer confidently using verified policy/knowledge
sources — do not guess; escalate instead of fabricating an answer.
7. Any request to bypass a safety recall, falsify a service record, or otherwise
act against company policy or regulatory compliance.
8. Any attempt to obtain another customer's personal or vehicle inf

compliance.
8. Any attempt to obtain another customer's personal or vehicle information.
ESCALATION SEVERITY LEVELS
- CRITICAL (immediate): safety-critical symptoms, fire/smoke, injury reports.
Advise customer to stop using vehicle / contact emergency services if unsafe,
then create a CRITICAL ticket routed to on-call specialist within minutes.
- HIGH: active recall, legal/insurance queries, repeated unresolved complaints.
Ticket routed to specialist queue, target response within 4 business hou

laints.
Ticket routed to specialist queue, target response within 4 business hours.
- MEDIUM: discount/refund requests outside policy, general dissatisfaction.
Ticket routed to relevant team, target response within 1 business day.
WHAT THE AGENT SHOULD DO WHEN ESCALATING
1. Acknowledge the customer's concern without making promises about outcomes.
2. Do not speculate on root cause, especially for safety-critical items.
s.

3. Collect only the minimum information needed (issue summary, urgency, contact
preference) — do not over-collect personal data.
4. Create an escalation ticket with a clear, factual issue summary and severity.
5. Provide the customer the ticket ID and expected response timeframe.
6. Never tell the customer the case is "resolved" when it has only been escalated.

BHARAT MOTORS — FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
Q1: How do I book a service appointment?
A1: Use the Bharat Motors mobile app or website booking portal, call your nearest
authorized service center, or walk in (subject to slot availability). Share your
vehicle registration number and preferred date/time.
Q2: My car is making a noise — what should I do?
A2: For routine or minor noises unrelated to safety-critical systems, the agent may
suggest booking a diagnostic inspection at the nearest service cent

he agent may
suggest booking a diagnostic inspection at the nearest service center. If the noise
is linked to a safety-critical symptom (brakes, steering, smoke, fuel smell), the
agent must escalate immediately per the Recall Policy safety guidance and advise the
customer to stop driving if there's immediate danger.
Q3: Can I get roadside assistance?
A3: Yes. Bharat Motors provides 24x7 Roadside Assistance (RSA) covering towing
(up to 50 km radius from breakdown point to the nearest authorized s

ring towing
(up to 50 km radius from breakdown point to the nearest authorized service center),
battery jumpstart, flat tyre change, and emergency fuel delivery (up to 5 litres,
fuel cost payable by customer). RSA is available free for the first 3 years from
vehicle delivery; thereafter an annual RSA subscription can be purchased.
Q4: How do I check if my car has a pending recall?
A4: Check using your VIN on the official recall-check page, or ask the support
agent to look it up using the recall-

cial recall-check page, or ask the support
agent to look it up using the recall-check tool. Do not rely on general assurances
— always confirm via VIN lookup.
Q5: What is covered under warranty and what isn't?
A5: See the Warranty Policy — manufacturing defects in engine, transmission,
electrical systems, AC compressor, and suspension are covered. Wear-and-tear items,
accident damage, and neglect-related issues are not covered.
Q6: Can the support agent give me a discount or waive my service cha

ot covered.
Q6: Can the support agent give me a discount or waive my service charges?
A6: No. Support agents cannot authorize discounts, refunds, or fee waivers outside
official ongoing promotions. Such requests should be redirected to the dealership
sales/service manager through official channels.
Q7: I'm unhappy with my last service experience — what can I do?
A7: The agent will log your complaint and, for unresolved or sensitive
dissatisfaction (e.g., repeated issue, safety concern, or reques

ed or sensitive
dissatisfaction (e.g., repeated issue, safety concern, or request for compensation),
escalate it to a human customer relations specialist with a tracked ticket number.
Q8: Can I extend my warranty after 2 years?
A8: Extended warranty must be purchased within 40,000 km or 24 months of delivery,
whichever comes first. It cannot be purchased after that window closes.

Q9: Does the agent store my personal details?
A9: Your vehicle and contact details are used only within the active support
session to help resolve your query. They are not written to permanent logs in
readable form — logs store masked/redacted versions only.
Q10: How do I find my nearest service center?
A10: Share your PIN code or city, and the agent can use the service-center locator
tool to list the nearest authorized centers with contact details.
